system.summary: The Brulart de Leon cipher of 1615-18: letter-like signs with homophones, numbers with a virgule or an overbar for words and syllables, dotted vowels for princes, delete and repeat signs; key reconstructed by Satoshi Tomokiyo.
system.sibling_key: same cipher in the other letters to Brulart de Leon in BnF fr. 18043 and fr. 18044 (Tomokiyo)
system.notes: System fields from Tomokiyo's key table (DOC file on R2785/R2786, louisxiii.htm), not checked here. Split 14 Oct 2026 from louis1615 (the 1631 Sabran cipher is now sabran1631).

prior_solution.where: DECODE R2785/R2786 (Tomokiyo, Aug 2021) and cryptiana louisxiii.htm "Brulart de Leon"

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record views for R2785 and R2786, one image of each and the key file with the shared cookie.

Checked Tomokiyo's louisxiii.htm (DECODE's pointer): the Brulart de Leon cipher of 1615-18 reconstructed by him, both letters read with it (DECODE 'Partially decrypted', 2021); the residue probably nulls or cancelled signs. Entry closed without applying the key.

Split from the former combined target louis1615 (catalogue 191) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R2785/R2786 (the Brulart de Leon cipher, Tomokiyo's key) and R2748 (the 1631 Sabran cipher, Lasry's solution) are different ciphers. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps kept as recorded.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Tomokiyo's readings linked by URL (DECODE R2785, R2786; cryptiana louisxiii.htm); no transcription or local decryption exists in the repository (project work).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): no text of R2785 or R2786 is in the repository, and cryptiana louisxiii.htm gives the key and remarks on undeciphered symbols, not the letters. Both relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read; method read from existing decipherment -> not solved.

outcome.method_basis: Satoshi Tomokiyo reconstructed the Brulart de Leon key (1615-18) and attached it to both DECODE records, but no plaintext of either letter is published or in the repository, so no reading is claimed (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); with his key applied the method would be read with known key.
outcome.notes: Tomokiyo leaves some symbols undeciphered (probably nulls or cancelled signs, per his DECODE notes); not re-checked here. Nothing new about the text. Catalogue entry 191 removed 21 Sept 2026. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no plaintext of either letter exists in the repository or on Tomokiyo's page; both decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read, method -> not solved.

texts.label: Poitiers?, 15 Sep 1615
texts.summary: Louis XIII, countersigned by Brûlart de Sillery, to Léon Brûlart, his ambassador in Venice: clear French with cipher runs (contemporary decipherments above them mention 'Marini', 'retirer a Gennes', 'domestiques', 'aucun ombrage'); the King is still held in the town by his eldest sister's illness, which fits the court at Poitiers in September 1615. The reading is Satoshi Tomokiyo's, with his key, on DECODE R2785 and cryptiana louisxiii.htm.
texts.note: Tomokiyo's key is on the record, but no plaintext is in the repository or on his page (key image and remarks only); one page image (main checkout targets/louis1615/decode/IMG_R2785_I17344_P1.jpg) shows contemporary decipherments over most cipher runs; not counted as a reading (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: fetch the record's pages with the DECODE cookie and read them with his key and the interlinear glosses.

texts.label: Paris, 25 Jul 1617
texts.summary: Louis XIII (countersigned Brûlart de Sillery) to Léon Brûlart, ambassador in Venice; read by Satoshi Tomokiyo with his reconstructed Brûlart de Léon key (1615-18). Its contents are not described in the repository; only the address leaf was fetched.
texts.note: Tomokiyo's key is on the record, but no plaintext is in the repository or on his page (key image and remarks only); only the address leaf was fetched; not counted as a reading (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: fetch the record's pages with the DECODE cookie and read them with his key.
